source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
finding: After a failed trial the agent writes a first-person reflection, stores it in an episodic buffer and retries. This is a modern failure-driven loop: explain the failure, store it, use it next time.
numbers: ALFWorld, 134 tasks: ReAct+Reflexion solved 130 of 134 within 12 trials; ReAct alone stalled between trials 6 and 7 with a 22% hallucination rate. HotPotQA 100 questions: +20 points. HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80%.
limits: Success needs an external binary or test signal. Memory held only 1 to 3 reflections.
agent_relevance: Core pattern for our lessons-with-traps store: reflect only after a verified failure, keep few, keep them short.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion, ablations
finding: Written self-reflection beat plain episodic memory of the last trajectory. In code, dropping the explanation step gave no gain over baseline, and dropping test generation made things worse.
numbers: HotPotQA CoT(GT): self-reflection +8 points absolute over episodic memory alone. HumanEval-Rust hardest 50 (GPT-4): base 0.60; no tests 0.52; tests but no self-reflection 0.60; full Reflexion 0.68.
limits: Small ablation (50 problems). The Rust compiler gives rich error text.
agent_relevance: The explanation of the failure carries the gain, as Schank and Hammond predicted. A failure memory without a diagnosis adds nothing.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion, WebShop limitation (appendix B.1)
finding: On WebShop (100 environments) Reflexion showed no improvement after four trials and its reflections were not helpful. The authors say it cannot solve tasks needing diverse exploration.
numbers: 100 WebShop environments, stopped after 4 trials with no learning signal.
limits: Two-shot ReAct+Reflexion on a GPT-3 class model only.
agent_relevance: Boundary: failure lessons help when the fix is a small change of plan, not when the fix needs creative search. Do not expect lessons to replace exploration.

source: Zhao et al. (2023) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: ExpeL gathers success and failure experiences, compares fail/success pairs of the same task to extract natural-language insights with ADD, EDIT, UPVOTE and DOWNVOTE operations, and also retrieves similar successful trajectories.
numbers: Insights-only vs retrieve-only: HotpotQA 36% vs 31%; ALFWorld 50% vs 55%; WebShop 37% vs 38%. ExpeL in one attempt on ALFWorld 54% vs Reflexion 59% at R3; ExpeL+Reflexion over R0-R3: 54.5, 57.5, 59.7, 60.4 (as read; one table row is garbled in the text extraction).
limits: Insight list grows and retrieval of insights gets hard as it lengthens. Few seeds.
agent_relevance: Voting operators on a lessons list is a cheap way to prune bad lessons. Abstract insights help reasoning tasks; concrete cases help action tasks.

source: Zhao et al. (2023) ExpeL ablations on insight extraction
finding: Insights learned by the agent beat hand-written ones. Adding Reflexion-style reflections into insight extraction made results worse, because reflections sometimes hallucinate and mislead. A stronger insight model helped.
numbers: HotpotQA ablation (table 3): learned insights better than human-crafted; reflections added lower; gpt-4 extractor better than gpt-3.5. Transfer HotpotQA to FEVER: ReAct 58, ExpeL transfer 65 or 70 (table cells partly garbled).
limits: Exact cell alignment of table 1 and 3 is uncertain in the text extraction.
agent_relevance: A reflection is a hypothesis, not a fact. Compare a failure against a success of the same task before promoting a lesson.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: scaling agent self-evolving with reasoning memory
finding: Stores short strategy items (title, description, content) distilled from both successes and failures, labelled by an LLM judge. Failures yield preventive lessons. Memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS) adds contrast between parallel attempts.
numbers: WebArena overall success +8.3, +7.2, +4.6 points vs no memory across three backbones; Gemini-2.5-flash WebArena: Multi subset 6.9 no memory vs 13.8 ReasoningBank vs 20.7 with MaTTS. Up to 16% fewer steps.
limits: Judge accuracy was 72.7% on the Shopping subset. Simple embedding retrieval only. Backbones are Gemini and Claude 3.7.
agent_relevance: Closest modern match to Kolodner-style indexed failure lessons. Strategy-level lessons transfer better than raw trajectories.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: failure ablation
finding: Adding failure traces to memory helped ReasoningBank but did not help baselines that store success routines; for one baseline it hurt. How the failure is written matters.
numbers: WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash: Synapse 40.6 to 41.7 with failures; AWM 44.4 to 42.2; ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7.
limits: One subset, single run per cell.
agent_relevance: Do not dump raw failed trajectories into memory. Distil them into a cause and an avoidance rule first.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025) ReasoningBank: robustness to noisy failure labels
finding: Memory quality held up when the success/failure judge was made worse by simulation, with the best result at perfect labels.
numbers: Simulated judge accuracy 100% down to 50%: success rate about 50.6 at the top and about 47.6 at 50%; flat within 70 to 90%.
limits: Simulated label flips, one subset (Shopping). Real judge accuracy was 72.7%.
agent_relevance: Outcome labels need not be perfect for lesson storage, but a verified outcome still gives the best lessons.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: fine-tuning LLM agents without fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Explicit case-based reasoning agent: a case bank of (state, action, reward) tuples holding successes and failures, retrieved by similarity or a learned Q-function, with GPT-4.1 as planner.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3, test 79.40%. DeepResearcher avg F1 59.9 (K=0) to 63.6 (K=1), flat at 63.9 to 64.5 for K=4 to 32. Five iterations: no CBR 78.65 to 84.47; non-parametric CBR 79.84 to 84.85; parametric 80.46 to 85.44. Out-of-distribution gain 4.7 to 9.6 points.
limits: Gain of CBR over no CBR shrinks to under 1 point by iteration 5. No ablation isolates the failure cases.
agent_relevance: Retrieving few cases (K=1 to 4) is enough. More cases add nothing. Keep lessons short and few.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Induces reusable workflows only from past examples judged correct by an evaluator. Failures are not stored; the authors warn that wrong induced workflows can degrade performance.
numbers: Relative success +24.6% on Mind2Web and +51.1% on WebArena. Mind2Web cross-domain step SR: offline 32.6 vs online 35.5 (as read).
limits: Success-only memory, the opposite design of failure-driven CBR, so it serves as a contrast case.
agent_relevance: Use as the control: success routines versus failure lessons.

source: An et al. (2023) Learning from mistakes makes LLM better reasoner (LEMA)
finding: Fine-tunes on pairs of wrong reasoning with GPT-4 corrections: mistake step, explanation, corrected answer. Ablations show the explanation and the corrected solution matter.
numbers: LLaMA-2-70B: GSM8K 83.5 vs 81.4 CoT-only; MATH 25.0 vs 23.6; with correction-centric evolution MATH 29.3; CSQA 85.3 vs 84.2. Gains held at equal data size for 4 of 5 models, not for LLaMA-2-7B.
limits: This is training, not a scaffold. The corrector was GPT-4.
agent_relevance: Supports the lesson format: wrong step, why wrong, correct step. Weak models learn less from mistakes.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet
finding: Without outside feedback, self-correction lowers accuracy. Gains reported by Reflexion-style work come from oracle labels that tell the model when to stop.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after round 1; GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7 (round 2); GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after 2 rounds. With oracle labels GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 95.5, HotpotQA 26 to 49. On GSM8K GPT-3.5 kept its first answer 74.7% of the time.
limits: Single-pass correction, not a stored cross-task lesson. HotpotQA sample is 100.
agent_relevance: Key trap: a failure signal must be external. Only store a lesson when a check or test confirmed the failure.

source: Li, Yang and Ettinger (2024) When hindsight is not 20/20
finding: Single-round self-reflection with no external feedback helped on TruthfulQA but was about 4% worse on HotpotQA. It helps most when first answers are mostly wrong and the question is hard; it harms when half or more of the candidates were right.
numbers: GPT-3.5, K=4 samples per question; HotpotQA about 4 points below exploration-only and standard prompting. Similar pattern with LLaMA-2 and Mixtral.
limits: Reflection over candidate answers, not a failure memory across tasks.
agent_relevance: Gate reflection on evidence that the first answer is likely wrong, such as low agreement across samples.

source: Xing et al. (2024) Understanding the weakness of LLM agents within a complex Android environment
finding: In an Android benchmark, Reflexion did not beat simply re-executing failed tasks without reflection. The authors blame reflections that bias the agent or are not used.
numbers: Reflexion@5 vs Re-execute@5 on cross-app tasks with GPT-3.5 and GPT-4: no gain from reflection. A count-based exploration hint gave 27% improvement on the Camera app (GPT-4).
limits: Single benchmark; long trajectories with repeated actions give poor material for reflection.
agent_relevance: A failed replication of the Reflexion gain. Retry alone may be enough in some domains, so test reflection against plain retry.

source: Dixit, Kamal and Oates (2026) Honest lying: memory confabulation in reflexive agents
finding: Reflexion-style memories can freeze on a wrong diagnosis repeated every trial. Binary pass/fail feedback produces this most; specific feedback (unit tests) least.
numbers: Existing logs, gpt-3.5-turbo: frozen memory in ALFWorld 32% (16/50, RRR 0.64), WebShop 82% (55/67), HotpotQA 46% (46/100), HumanEval 17% (4/23). Frozen envs took 7.6 trials vs 1.5; r=0.808. 0 of 121 reflections named the correct object. Two memory-harmful envs: solved in 1 trial without memory, 7 and 8 trials with it.
limits: Mostly gpt-3.5; mitigation solved only 3 of 16 frozen envs, and 14 of 16 were capability-limited anyway.
agent_relevance: A false lesson persists and is acted on. Add lesson expiry and a check that the lesson matches the trace.

source: Dixit et al. (2026) Honest lying: mitigation
finding: Replacing free self-diagnosis with parsed trace facts (actions that got 'Nothing happens', repeated actions) raised correct-object mentions and cut repetition.
numbers: Object mention 0% to 86% (134/156); RRR 0.64 to 0.10; solved 3/16 vs 2/16 with no memory. HumanEval: 18/18 reflections name the error type; RRR 0.59 to 0.44; one regression (HumanEval/77).
limits: Small sample; same gpt-3.5 setup.
agent_relevance: Ground each lesson in quoted trace evidence: failed step, root cause, new plan.

source: Zhu et al. (2025) Where LLM agents fail and how they can learn from failures (AgentDebug)
finding: Builds an error taxonomy (memory, reflection, planning, action, system), a 200-trajectory benchmark and a debugger that finds the earliest critical error and gives targeted feedback for retry.
numbers: Critical-error all-correct accuracy 24.3% vs 0.3% for the best baseline; step accuracy 45.0% vs 28.0%; up to 26% relative gain in task success on ALFWorld, GAIA, WebShop.
limits: Counterfactual replay needs a simulator; the benchmark is only 200 trajectories.
agent_relevance: Record the earliest failing step, not the last one. Error cascade is the main failure source.

source: Hammond (1986/1989) CHEF case-based planning, as summarised by Davies
finding: CHEF retrieves a recipe, adapts it, simulates it, explains any failure causally, picks a repair strategy from a failure-type packet, and stores predictive links so the failure is anticipated in later plans.
numbers: Worked example: soggy broccoli in beef-and-broccoli. 20 known repair packets; 3 strategies for the relevant packet; beef generalised to meat, broccoli to vegetables. No test-set numbers.
limits: Hand-built domain rules; failures from several interacting causes cannot be blamed on one item; some repairs are too complex to store. Secondary summary, not the paper.
agent_relevance: The original design: explain, repair, index so the failure is predicted before it happens. Our store needs cause, repair and trigger condition.

source: Hammond (1986) CHEF: a model of case-based planning (AAAI-86 abstract page)
finding: Plans are indexed by the goals they meet and the problems they avoid, and failures are indexed by the world features that predict them.
numbers: No quantitative results on the page.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Index lessons by what predicts the trap, not by topic.

source: Hammond (1987) Explaining and repairing plans that fail (IJCAI-87)
finding: Search-listed: causal explanation of a failure selects repair strategies, and the same explanation builds the anticipation link.
numbers: none read
limits: Only the search snippet was seen this session.
agent_relevance: Same as CHEF; read before building the lesson schema.

source: Schank (1982) Dynamic memory; Schank and Leake (1989) Creativity and learning in a case-based explainer
finding: Memory is failure-driven: a failed expectation triggers reminding of an earlier case and drives learning. Explanation patterns are reused and repaired where they do not fit (SWALE project).
numbers: none read
limits: Only search summaries were seen; the PDF fetch failed this session.
agent_relevance: Supports retrieving a lesson at the moment an expectation breaks, not at the start of a task.

source: Yin and Leake (2026) Capturing LLM cases for RAG reuse (ICCBR workshop)
finding: Stores query, answer and feedback as cases on MMLU subsets and retrieves them as context. One round of feedback helps; a second round does not reliably help.
numbers: McNemar tests: 4 trials significant for single feedback vs baseline; 3 trials double better than single; 6 trials double lower than single (not significant). Test case: gpt-4.1-nano history set, 687 questions.
limits: Initial work. Authors note that double feedback stores only successful cases, which removes negative cases.
agent_relevance: Small sign that negative cases matter: dropping them lowered accuracy in some cells.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Retroformer: retrospective large language agents with policy gradient optimization
finding: A small retrospective model is trained by policy gradient to write failure summaries (root cause plus plan) that tune a frozen actor's prompt.
numbers: Reported gains over Reflexion-type baselines: HotPotQA +18% with 4 retries, AlfWorld +36% with 3 retries, WebShop +4%.
limits: Needs fine-tuning of the reflector; the small WebShop gain matches the Reflexion WebShop limit. Only the abstract and intro were read closely.
agent_relevance: Learned reflection quality helps, but it requires training, which our scaffold excludes.

source: Hatalis, Kondapalli and Christou (2025) Review of CBR for LLM agents
finding: Review that maps the CBR cycle (retrieve, reuse, revise, retain) onto LLM agents and notes that introspection can tell retrieval failure from adaptation failure.
numbers: No new measurements. Cites work where CBR cut seven failure modes of LLM code generation versus zero-shot and static few-shot prompts.
limits: Theory and survey; second-hand result.
agent_relevance: Useful split when a lesson fails: was the wrong case retrieved or was it applied wrongly?

source: Zhu et al. (2025) AgentDebug rollout comparison on ALFWorld
finding: Compared rollout styles zero-shot: ReAct, Reflection, Act-only, Memory+ReAct and a modular strategy; plain memory gave small gains.
numbers: Memory+ReAct 0.34 vs ReAct 0.26 success in the figure read.
limits: Read from a garbled figure; approximate.
agent_relevance: Memory without diagnosis adds little, again.
